title: Electronic properties and topological aspects of graphene nanohelicoids
authors: Xiaoqian Liu, Arsen Herasymchuk, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Oleg V. Yazyev
abstract: We introduce graphene nanohelicoids, geometric analogues of graphene nanoribbons, in which the honeycomb lattice is embedded on a helicoidal surface. Starting from the three-dimensional helical structure, we construct effective one-dimensional lattice models with band structures characterized by a momentum-shifted particle-hole relation $E_v(k)=-E_c(k+π)$ that reflects an anti-chiral symmetry arising from the nonsymmorphic symmetry. A systematic investigation of graphene nanohelicoids using the tight-binding approximation reveals a number of trends upon varying width and edge orientation, for instance, alternating transitions between semiconducting and metallic regimes. As the structure width varies, the band gap periodically closes and reopens, accompanied by an alternating Zak phase that switches between trivial and nontrivial. We derive an analytic tight-binding model and introduce a continuous deformation of the graphene nanohelicoids that explains the origin of width-dependent band inversion and alternating Zak phase.
summary: This paper theoretically examines graphene nanohelicoids by modeling their electronic structure using a tight-binding approach that incorporates anti-chiral symmetry. Key findings show that the band gap oscillates periodically with width, and the topological invariant (Zak phase) alternates between trivial and nontrivial states. This work provides deep insight into how geometric curvature dictates the fundamental quantum electronic properties of 2D materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the electronic properties and topological characteristics of graphene nanohelicoids (GNHs), which are structures where the honeycomb lattice is curved onto a helicoidal surface.
main_result: The band gap size in GNHs exhibits periodic closing and reopening as the width changes, accompanied by an alternating Zak phase that switches between trivial and nontrivial values.
method: The authors employed the tight-binding approximation to derive effective one-dimensional lattice models from the 3D helical structure, supplemented by mathematical derivations involving recurrence relations for associated polynomials.
model_or_system: The physical system is Graphene Nanohelicoids (GNHs). The model uses an effective 1D tight-binding Hamiltonian exhibiting anti-chiral symmetry ($E_v(k)=-E_c(k+\pi)$), contrasting with standard chiral symmetries.
key_observables: Band structure, Zak phase, band gap size, and the spectral relation $E_v(k) = -E_c(k + \pi)$.
important_parameters: Structure width ($W$), edge termination (zigzag vs. armchair), and momentum shift ($\pi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily uses the tight-binding approximation, considering only intralayer coupling, and relies on deriving analytic models for the effective 1D chain.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the GNH lattice model, compare band structures under anti-chiral vs. chiral constraints, and show how gap dependence varies with width or radius changes for zigzag and armchair edges.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the electronic structure by first establishing the effective 1D model and symmetry properties (anti-chiral). It then details results based on edge termination (zigzag vs. armchair), concluding with advanced mathematical derivations concerning determinants and topological invariants using recurrence relations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter topology, the concept of engineered geometric constraints leading to protected electronic states (like those derived from symmetry) is highly relevant to designing quantum materials for novel quantum devices.
